_about: Campaign Manager playbook for the first Reign motion. Keys from the stub are kept as-is. Anything the stub left empty or undefined has a sibling '_guess' key explaining my assumption. The reign_gate MCP server reads this file at runtime.
_guess_version: Stub doesn't say how playbooks version. Guess: semver per playbook. Every audit record stores playbook_id + version, so you can prove which rules were live when an action happened. Changing approvers or kill criteria = minor bump; changing audience or trigger = new playbook.
_guess_status: Not in the stub. 'armed' = drafts and internal handoffs allowed, nothing goes to the account. Other values: 'live', 'paused', 'killed'.

audience._guess_audience: icp_id + segment come from the stub. The playbook POINTS to the shared ICP instead of copying it, so a new launch swaps these two fields and nothing else. 'financial_services' is repeated here so the gate knows R-17 is required without re-reading the ICP. Lanes come from Paul: 'Route them without asking.'

trigger.angle: SR 26-2 excludes generative and agentic AI from its scope; brief the audit gap that leaves.

trigger._note: Fallback trigger, not built this round.

_guess_trigger: Stub shows one trigger object. Guess: a list, because Paul names two for the bank (SR 26-2, DORA) and one playbook shouldn't be cloned per regulation. Each trigger can be switched off on its own.
_guess_channel: Stub lists 'briefing' but doesn't define it. Guess: a Reign-produced, sourced brief handed to the internal account owner, PLUS a calendar hold for the Executive Assurance Briefing. Not a Calendly link sent cold, and not an email sequence. Nothing goes to the account until the briefing is booked (Paul's rule).

approval.trigger_exception: brief may go to the internal account owner only
approval._guess_approval: Stub says only that approval must name a human if the channel can send. Split into 'principals' (who authorized this CLASS of action, per R-17) and 'approvers' (who approves each individual send). The gate rejects anyone not on these lists.

kill_criteria.rule: any agent action without an audit record
2 or more briefs rejected by the approver as inaccurate or generic
0 briefings booked after 10 briefs handed off
any brief addressed to a segment not active in the ICP

_guess_kill_criteria: Stub: 'kill_criteria is how CRO stops a motion that goes sloppy.' Guess: named rules with a set action. The CRO flips kill_switch; the gate then blocks every action, which is tested. No email-style metrics (bounce, open rate) because this motion doesn't send email.

audit._guess_audit: Stub: 'audit should satisfy R-17 when the audience is FS.' Fields are R-17's list. 'on_by_default' for non-FS follows Paul's stricter rule: 'If you cannot leave an audit trail, it does not send.'

next_swap._note: Paul's 'one playbook we can reuse on the next product launch': change these two fields; gate, skill and evals stay the same. Verify PCCP scope first (applies to AI-enabled medical devices, not pharma broadly).
